newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares post gains in bourse, ignore Siemens.
newsitem.headline: German shares post gains in bourse, ignore Siemens.

text.p: Germany's DAX share index shrugged off weakness in one of its heavyweight shares to post solid gains in bourse trade, drawing strength from overnight Wall Street gains and the firmer dollar.
The 30-share DAX index ended up 55.62 points at 3,395.95 points and maintained the gains in post-bourse IBIS electronic dealings as the index was up 47.52 points at 3,396.42 points.
The index rose despite electronics group Siemens AG reported flat first-half results for its 1996/97 business year and gave a muted outlook for the balance of the year.
Siemens shares, among the most heavily-traded during the day, ended bourse trade down 2.30 marks at 88.90 marks.
"The figures were disappointing simply because they were in line with expectations," said one trader, noting the stock had risen strongly in recent days ahead of the results.
But a firmer dollar, which was trading above 1.71 marks in European dealings, helped to spur the gains along with the dramatic overnight Wall Street advance.
Traders said dealings in the afternoon and on Thursday would depend on movements in New York amid a lack of fresh fundamentals to influence the German market.

Among other shares, preference shares in haircare products group Wella AG ended up 75 marks at 1,030 marks as Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said it had raised its recommendation in the stock to "overweight" from "neutral".
Wella said on Tuesday it expected 1997 net profits to climb 25 percent, with sales up seven percent.

Airline Lufthansa continued to rise as dealers cited strong technical factors and a general positive mood surrounding recent fundamentals in the stock, notably its continuing restructuring to boost profits.
Lufthansa shares ended up 90 pfennigs at 23.80 marks.
Auto shares were mostly higher in line with the market as dealers said the sector's rally, recently interrupted by a small pause, may now be back on track.
BMW gained 28.50 marks to 1,397.50 but later ended the session up nine marks at 1,380 marks. Daimler-Benz AG rose 2.65 marks to 130.35 and Volkswagen ended up 34 marks at 1,092.50.
